evidence.quote: Today the Federal Open Market Committee decided to raise the target range for the federal funds rate by ¼ percentage point, bringing it to ½ to ¾ percent.
We continue to expect that the evolution of the economy will warrant only gradual increases in the federal funds rate over time to achieve and maintain our objectives.
Compared with the projections made in September, the median path for the federal funds rate has been revised up just ¼ percentage point.
We have a strong labor market, and we have a resilient economy.
Remember that inflation is still below our objective.
We’ve not yet made any precise decisions about when that will occur.

parsed.rationale: The Committee hikes rates, describes the labor market as strong and near maximum employment, and revises the projected rate path slightly upward. Tightening is tempered by emphasis on a gradual pace, inflation still below goal, and no near-term change to reinvestment.
